original_analysis.analysis_summary: The log sequence shows a rapid chain of suspicious activities on WORKSTATION5. An audit log was cleared (EventID 1102), followed by the creation of a known evasion tool (ProcessHerpaderping.exe) that immediately spawns mimikatz and a custom binary (wardog.exe). The custom binary loads mimikatz (identified by its image hash and description). Privileged service calls (SeTcbPrivilege) and handle duplication events occur, and the attacker writes to the BAM service registry key to establish persistence. Multiple registry accesses to LSA and other security‑related keys are observed. The timeline demonstrates these events happening within seconds, indicating a coordinated attack.
original_analysis.agent_reasoning:
1. EventID 1102 indicates the security audit log was cleared, a classic anti‑forensic move. 2. EventID 4688 shows ProcessHerpaderping.exe being executed with a command line that references mimikatz.exe, a credential‑dumping tool. 3. Shortly after, wardog.exe is created (EventID 4688) and its image load (EventID 7) is identified as mimikatz, confirming credential‑dumping activity. 4. Registry writes to HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\bam\State\UserSettings (EventID 13) are typical persistence mechanisms used by malware. 5. Privileged service calls (EventID 4673) with SeTcbPrivilege and handle duplication (EventID 4690) suggest the attacker is elevating privileges and manipulating handles to hide activity. 6. Repeated accesses to the LSA registry key (EventIDs 4656, 4658, 4663) indicate attempts to read or modify security policy. 7. The timeline built around ProcessHerpaderping.exe shows all these events occurring within a few seconds, confirming a coordinated attack.

All EventIDs were validated with the event_id_extractor tool. No encoded PowerShell commands were present, so the decoder tool was not required.
